# Skills

Skills are focused instruction sets for a specific kind of work. Each canonical skill folder contains a final `SKILL.md` and any support files; `scripts/sync.sh` builds the agent-specific outputs and reference tables in this repository. The `agent-config` maintenance skill stays repo-local, so it is not installed for other projects.

## How Claude and Codex find skills

Claude and Codex use the same canonical skill folders, and both mostly choose a skill from its description, so write an action-led sentence that starts with `Use this skill when...`. Claude also has one path-scoped rule, `src/adapters/claude/rules/code-style.md`, that asks it to load the code-style skill when it works with code files.

Claude reads shared skills from `~/.claude/skills/`, while Codex reads them from `~/.agents/skills/`. Claude also provides built-in skills managed by Claude Code; those skills have no source files in this repository.

## Keep the skill list within budget

`scripts/validate/check-skill-list.sh` estimates the Codex list shown for installed skills. It counts each skill's name, description and installed path at one token per four bytes, rounded up per line. Skills listed in `scripts/skill-exclusions.txt` are excluded. The report shows the current size, the recorded limit and the room left in Codex's full 5,440-token skill-list budget. The installed path uses the current machine's home directory, so the measured count can differ on a machine with a different home path length.

The recorded limit starts at the current size. After merging a skill family, lower `SKILL_LIST_LIMIT` in the check to the new measured count. To raise it deliberately, change that value and explain why the extra list space is needed in the review. The check also finds broken relative links in skill guides, reference files that no guide or other reference links to, and retired skill names left in maintained source. It skips the unlinked-reference check for upstream skill folders that contain `SOURCE.md`; their links are still checked. Add each merged-away name to `RETIRED_SKILL_NAMES` in the same script.

## Built-in Claude Code skills

For built-in skills, see the [official Claude Code documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills).

## Control skill loading

Use `skillOverrides` in `settings.json` to reduce the skills listing and control which skills are available to the model. This is the main tool for reducing token usage, as skill descriptions are the bulk of the listing cost.

| Value                   | Effect                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"on"`                  | Full description shown; the skill is available for automatic and manual use                                   |
| `"name-only"`           | Skill name shown without its description, so it doesn't consume description tokens; `/skill-name` still works |
| `"user-invocable-only"` | Hidden from automatic matching; `/skill-name` still works                                                     |
| `"off"`                 | Hidden from automatic matching and manual use                                                                 |

To re-enable a skill suppressed by a parent settings file, set it to `"on"` in the project or local settings file:

```json
{
	"skillOverrides": {
		"typescript": "on"
	}
}
```

Nothing creates a local `.claude/settings.json` by default. Prefer `AGENTS.md` and ordinary docs for repo-specific guidance, and agent-run for project command registrations.

## Add a new skill

1. Create a grouped folder for the skill, using its domain and slug:

    ```text
    skills/my-group/my-skill/
    ```

2. Add `SKILL.md` with front matter used for discovery and generated tables:

    ```markdown
    ---
    name: my-skill
    description: >
        Use this skill when doing this work.
    ---

    # My skill

    Content here.
    ```

3. Add any support files the skill needs beside `SKILL.md`.

4. Run `scripts/sync.sh` to refresh the skill table in this file and rebuild the Claude and Codex outputs.

5. Run `bash scripts/validate.sh` to check generated output and markers before you install the skill.

The skill-manifest check also rejects front-matter keys outside the Agent Skills standard list and the allowed `disable-model-invocation` runtime extension.

After `scripts/setup.sh`, shared skills are available to Claude via `~/.claude/skills/` and to Codex via `~/.agents/skills/`.
To leave out a skill, list its folder name in `scripts/skill-exclusions.txt`. See [install the agent configuration](setup.md#install-the-agent-configuration) to check what is installed.
